# DocumentedArgumentType

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Report an argument that breaks a parameter's contract when PHPDoc is taken
into account: the `@param` type of a project function rejects it, or the
declared type rejects a value whose type only PHPDoc describes. PHP may run
such a call, but the code and its documentation disagree. Mismatches the
code alone proves are InvalidArgumentType's.

## Example

```php{7,11}
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

class Order {}
/** @param Order $order */
function archive($order) {}
archive('order-1');

function charge(int $cents) {}
/** @param string $amount */
function bill($amount) { charge($amount); }
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 7: Pass Order to $order of archive(), not string.</li>
<li>line 11: Pass int to $cents of charge(), not string.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Calls, argument binding and callee resolution as InvalidArgumentType
  defines them.
- The type of the argument is the one PHPDoc-aware inference gives:
  `@param`, `@var` and `@return` tags count.
- Every declaration the call may bind to rejects every value of the
  argument's type, through the declared type of the parameter or, for a
  function of the project, its `@param` type. A null default makes either
  type nullable.
- The weak-mode conversions and the exceptions of InvalidArgumentType
  apply alike.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Arguments InvalidArgumentType reports: the declared types reject
  what the code alone shows.
- The `@param` type of a variadic parameter, of a parameter of PHP's
  own functions, a `@param` type naming templates, and a `@param` type the
  declared type rejects (a stale tag).
- The value details of a `@param` type: integer ranges, string
  lengths and literal string values. `@param positive-int` accepts any
  integer.
- Every exception of InvalidArgumentType.

## Fix

None: either the call or the documentation is wrong.

## PHP versions

All versions, as InvalidArgumentType.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DocumentedArgumentType": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DocumentedArgumentType
```
